newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Anti-APEC group beaten back but toast "success".
newsitem.headline: Anti-APEC group beaten back but toast "success".

text.p: It was not quite the Long March but advancing to within 20 kms (12 miles) of the APEC summit venue was deemed victory enough and the protesters toasted their success by singing revolutionary songs.
"People united will never be defeated," thousands of leftist protesters chanted after forcing their way through seven police blockades before calling off a bid to reach the summit site.
Exhausted, they flopped on the streets beside policemen who dropped their truncheons and shields after keeping pace with the protesters for nearly 30 hours.

Occasional rousing cries of "Long live international solidarity" sent the some 7,000 protesters into fresh bursts of activity as they cheered those who led their 460-vehicle caravan of jeepneys -- the popular Filipino vehicle designed after World War Two jeeps.
About 100 foreign delegates participated in the protest calvacade, which left Manila on Sunday.

The cavalcade, organised to protest against the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum's goal of liberalising trade on grounds it would negatively affect poorer countries, had planned to drive into Subic where the APEC leaders were meeting.

But after driving two-thirds of the way to San Fernando town, the protesters abandoned their cars and marched through heat and rain to Dinalupihan, where a larger force of 2,000 riot policemen completely sealed off the only route to the summit venue.
They retreated rather than risk what their leaders said would have been a suicidal confrontation.
"Considering the large number of our enemy, we will not sacrifice our bodies, we will not sacrifice our force because that will be suicide," leftist leader Nathaniel Santiago told the protesters.
By Monday afternoon, the protesters decided to disperse.
Police officials escorting the cavalcade said they had let the protesters pass through the earlier blockades because they were instructed to show "maximum tolerance."
As the summit of leaders of APEC's 18 member economies ended shortly after 3.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), the weary leftist army started what looked to be an arduous journey back to Manila.
